facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of right upper abdominal pain
without nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever
no history of hepatitis, surgery, or hereditary disease, and no underlying medical conditions
afebrile and oriented
right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
no hepatosplenomegaly
negative Murphy’s sign and shifting dullness
AFP 2.4 µg/l (normal 0.0–7.0)
CEA 11.6 µg/l (normal 0.0–5.0)
a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe

concepts.why: Elevated CA19-9 and CEA levels, along with a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa, suggest intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
Right upper abdominal tenderness, negative Murphy’s sign, and gallbladder wall thickening indicate cholecystitis.
Gallstones are present, as indicated by ultrasonography and CT findings.

aliases: Enlarged lymph nodes in the liver hilum
concepts.why: Enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes suggest a possible malignancy, such as intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
A heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe is present, which could be a liver mass.
Mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation suggests a possible bile duct obstruction.
Elevated WBC count and right upper abdominal tenderness indicate an inflammatory process in the liver.
Elevated CA19-9 and CEA levels, along with a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa, suggest a neoplasm of the bile duct.

rationales.F01: Right upper abdominal pain is a common symptom of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and liver mass.
rationales.F05: Right upper abdominal tenderness is a common symptom of cholecystitis and gallstones.
rationales.F10: Elevated CA19-9 is a tumor marker for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and neoplasm of the bile duct.
rationales.F12: A heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa is a characteristic imaging finding of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and liver mass.
